description: Build ParaWave: a free, fully client-side static web app (GitHub Pages) that turns a handful of parameters into a live 3D/2D preview of sliced parametric wave wall art and exports one cut-ready SVG per slat for CNC/laser cutting. Stack: TypeScript strict · Svelte 5 (runes) · Three.js (raw) · Vite · Vitest · jszip. No backend, no analytics, no CDN at runtime. All geometry stored in mm internally; inch toggle is display-only (TS-D8). Determinism is within fit tolerance, not byte-identical (TS-D2). Target CAM is Carbide Create. See specs/ for PRD, SRS (REQUIREMENTS.md), TECH_SPEC.md, and DESIGN.md.

userStories.title: Project scaffold & tooling
userStories.description: Bootstrap the Vite + Svelte 5 + TypeScript project with CI, GitHub Pages deployment, self-hosted fonts, and the full src/ directory tree — so every subsequent milestone can build on a green pipeline.
acceptanceCriteria: Vite project with Svelte 5 + TypeScript template initialised; `vite dev` serves a blank page at the /ParaWave/ sub-path
tsconfig.json has `strict: true` and `noUncheckedIndexedAccess: true`
ESLint (TypeScript + Svelte rules) and Prettier configured; lint script passes on the empty project
Vitest configured; `vitest run` passes with at least one trivial test
GitHub Actions workflow: install → tsc --noEmit → lint → vitest run → vite build → deploy dist/ to gh-pages
Fraunces (woff2, weights 400/500/600) and IBM Plex Mono (woff2, weights 400/500) self-hosted with @font-face + font-display:swap; no Google Fonts request at runtime
src/ directory tree created: core/, core/wave/, core/fit/, worker/, three/, ui/, state/, export/ with index stubs that TypeScript resolves cleanly
userStories.notes: NFR-DEPLOY.1 requires fully static deployment to GitHub Pages at zero hosting cost. DESIGN §3.4 and NFR-PRIV.1 prohibit any runtime CDN/Google Fonts request — fonts must be subset to Latin + ° × → … ± and digits and bundled as woff2. Set Vite `base` to `/ParaWave/` in vite.config.ts so asset URLs resolve on the Pages sub-path. Worker must be imported via `new Worker(new URL('./geometry.worker.ts', import.meta.url), { type: 'module' })` for Vite to bundle it correctly (needed in PW-004).

userStories.title: Core types & unit system
userStories.description: Write the canonical TypeScript type definitions and the mm ↔ inch unit layer that everything else in the app depends on.
acceptanceCriteria: core/types.ts defines: Design, WaveConfig (discriminated union: diagonal | radial | interference), Source (discriminated union), FittedPath, BezierSeg, ComputeRequest, ComputeResult exactly as specified in TECH_SPEC §5.1 and §5.3

core/units.ts: stores all values in mm (canonical); formatForDisplay(mm, unit) converts to display string with correct decimal precision; parseFromDisplay never silently clamps; mm→inch→mm round-trip is lossless
`core/` imports nothing outside `core/` — no DOM, no Three.js, no Svelte
userStories.notes: FR-IN.2 and SRS §1.7-F: the unit toggle is display-only; geometry is always stored in mm. TS-D8 formalises this: emitted SVG coordinates are always mm at 4 dp regardless of displayUnit. The Design interface carries `displayUnit: Unit` for formatting purposes only. All dimensional fields (H, W, D, pMin, slatWidth, gap, fitTolerance, lambda, cx, cy) are numbers in mm. Angles (theta, phi) in degrees. Verification V-2: mm→inch→mm must return identical values (FR-IN.2).

userStories.title: Wave families — diagonal, radial, interference
userStories.description: Implement the three wave function families with analytic f(x,y) and ∂f/∂y, all obeying the [−1, 1] contract by construction.
acceptanceCriteria: core/wave/types.ts defines WaveField interface exposing f(x,y) and dfdy(x,y)
core/wave/diagonal.ts: f = sin(2π(x·cosθ + y·sinθ)/λ + φ), analytic ∂f/∂y; params are (θ, λ, φ) — NOT (λx, λy) (SRS §1.7-E)
core/wave/radial.ts: f = a(r)·sin(2π·r/λ + φ), exponential decay a(r)=exp(−k·r) with k derived from decay∈[0,1]; analytic ∂f/∂y with r=0 guard; center (cx,cy) may lie outside the piece
core/wave/interference.ts: weighted sum of K∈[1,8] diagonal or radial sources divided by Σ|weights|; derivative passthrough; |f| ≤ 1 guaranteed
core/wave/field.ts: factory building an evaluable WaveField from a WaveConfig
All families emit f ∈ [−1, 1] by construction (not by clamping) for any valid inputs
userStories.notes: FR-WAVE.1–.4. The [−1,1] contract is essential: it is what makes the protrusion map (FR-GEO.3) deterministic and design-independent — peaks always land exactly at D and troughs at pMin, with no clipping warning ever needed (FR-VAL.9). For radial: a(r)≤1 preserves the bound. For interference: dividing by Σ|weights| (not Σweights) preserves it even with mixed signs. FR-VAL.11 guarantees Σ|weights|>0 so division is always safe. The derivative ∂f/∂y is needed for exact Hermite tangents (PW-005); expose it from each family. Default landing design (SRS §1.7-H): interference K=2, src1 diagonal θ=30° λ=300mm, src2 radial centered λ=200mm, equal weights.

userStories.title: Geometry primitives & readouts
userStories.description: Implement fin-count, centerline, and protrusion-map formulas, plus the cheap derived readouts that update synchronously on the main thread.
acceptanceCriteria: core/geometry.ts: N = floor((W + gap) / (slatWidth + gap)); centerline array x_i = margin + slatWidth/2 + i·(slatWidth+gap) with margin = (W − span)/2; protrusion p(x,y) = pMin + (D−pMin)·(f+1)/2 using analytic ±1 bounds
core/readouts.ts: pure function Design → ReadoutValues returning N, spanned width, end margin, stock thickness, declared depth range (pMin/D), total footprint; recomputes live from any Design change
userStories.notes: FR-GEO.1–.4. The protrusion map uses analytic ±1 bounds — never observed extremes — so it is design-independent and deterministic (FR-GEO.3, FR-VAL.9: depth can never exceed D by construction). The array is centered: N slats span N·slatWidth + (N−1)·gap ≤ W with equal left/right end margins. slat_width and gap are never silently altered (FR-IN.5, FR-GEO.2). Readouts are the 'cheap' tier (TECH_SPEC §5.2 TS-D7): they must update synchronously on the main thread without waiting for the Worker, so exportEnabled and hard-block validation are always instant.

userStories.title: Curve-fit engine — analytic Hermite + adaptive subdivision
userStories.description: Implement the two-file curve-fit engine that produces the front-edge cubic-Bézier sequence for one fin, guaranteeing max deviation ≤ fitTolerance while remaining compact and deterministic.
acceptanceCriteria: core/fit/hermite.ts: given (p, dp/dy) at y0 and y1, computes the four Bézier control points of the analytic Hermite cubic: P1 = P0 + (h/3)·(dz/dy@y0, 1), P2 = P3 − (h/3)·(dz/dy@y1, 1)

core/fit/adaptive.ts: wavelength-tied seeding partitions [0,H] at multiples of λmin/SEED_PER_WAVELENGTH; hard seed boundaries injected at exact radial-center kinks (x_i == cx, IEEE double equality, 0≤cy≤H); recursive midpoint subdivision with MAX_DEPTH cap emits BezierSeg[] whose front-edge max deviation from p(x_i,y) is ≤ fitTolerance
Determinism: identical Design inputs always produce the same BezierSeg[] on the same JS engine (no randomness, no observed-extreme feedback)
userStories.notes: SRS §1.7-D, TECH_SPEC §6.3–6.4, TS-D3/D4. This is the technical heart of the app. Seeding is wavelength-tied to defeat midpoint-test aliasing on periodic fields — each seed segment spans less than half the shortest active wavelength. The kink rule (TS-D3) is strict: only inject a boundary when x_i == cx by IEEE double equality; fins merely near a center are genuinely smooth and the adaptive subdivision auto-densifies them. The midpoint error test: compute Bézier at the parameter corresponding to y-midpoint, compare its z to p(x_i, ym). Constants SEED_PER_WAVELENGTH and MAX_DEPTH are open issue OI-new — pick them so a worst-case short-λ design stays ≤ tolerance without pathological segment counts; validate via the M8 property test (PW-012, acceptance M8.3). TS-D2: determinism is within fit tolerance, not byte-identical across engines.

userStories.title: SVG emitter & validation engine
userStories.description: Write the SVG path emitter that produces one correct, scaled, closed slat path, and the pure validation function that classifies all Design states into typed issues.
acceptanceCriteria: core/svg.ts: returns an SVG string for one slat — one closed path with straight back/top/bottom edges as line segments and the fitted front edge as cubic Béziers; root <svg> carries width/height in mm AND viewBox '0 0 {D} {H}' (1 user unit = 1 mm); coordinates at fixed 4 decimal places; always emitted in mm regardless of displayUnit

core/validation.ts: pure function Design → ValidationResult with typed issues (field, tier, message); implements all FR-VAL.1–.11 conditions using the exact SRS-proposed message text; hard blocks: D≤pMin, slat+gap>W, any λ≤0, non-positive H/W/slatWidth, pMin<0, fitTolerance≤0, all-weights-zero; soft warnings: N>400, gap=0, segment count>threshold
userStories.notes: FR-EXP.1/.2/.9, TS-D8, FR-GEO.6, FR-VAL.1–.11. SVG orientation: height H along SVG +Y (Y-down authored per §1.7-B), straight back edge at X=0, wave front bulging toward +X (depth axis). The viewBox '0 0 {D} {H}' means the wave front can reach at most X=D — this is the 1u=1mm guarantee that Carbide Create depends on (§1.7-A, V-1). Validation uses the SRS's exact proposed wording verbatim — do not paraphrase. FR-IN.5: no silent clamping anywhere; invalid values are surfaced, never rewritten. FR-VAL.9: never emit a depth-clipping warning — it is impossible by construction (protrusion map uses analytic bounds). The segment-count soft warning (FR-VAL.8) threshold is a tunable constant (OI-6).

userStories.title: 3D mesh builder
userStories.description: Write the pure-core function that builds the single merged vertex/index buffer set (and per-fin range table) used by the Three.js scene.
acceptanceCriteria: core/mesh.ts: builds merged positions/indices/normals typed-array set from FittedPath[] by tessellating each fin's front-edge profile (y–z plane), closing the slat shape, and extruding along X by slatWidth; fins are placed at their x_i centerlines
finRanges: a Uint32Array of [start, count] pairs, one per fin, mapping face indices to fin indices for raycasting (used by three/picking.ts)
Output is one merged BufferGeometry worth of data — one draw call in Three.js
userStories.notes: TECH_SPEC §8.1, TS-D5. Both faces of each slat are identical (FR-GEO.5 — flat board, profile extruded straight). Normals are cheap to compute for a flat extrusion. The finRanges table enables binary-search raycasting in three/picking.ts (TS-D6). This function is called inside the Worker when needMesh:true; the Worker posts positions/indices/finRanges as transferables (zero-copy). mesh.ts lives in core/ and is therefore usable both in the Worker and in the main-thread synchronous fallback (TECH_SPEC §7.4).

userStories.title: Web Worker pipeline
userStories.description: Wrap the core/ pipeline in a Web Worker, add the single-in-flight bridge with latest-wins backpressure, and implement the synchronous main-thread fallback.
acceptanceCriteria: worker/geometry.worker.ts: thin host — receives ComputeRequest, runs field → adaptive fit → (mesh when needMesh:true), posts ComputeResult with positions/indices/finRanges as transferables; contains no geometry logic of its own
worker/bridge.ts: main-side bridge enforcing single-in-flight + pending-stash latest-wins (at most one request in flight; newest pending Design replaces any previously stashed one)
Bridge coalesces requests to ≤1 per animation frame (FR-VIZ.2)
If new Worker(...) throws or the Worker errors, bridge transparently switches to calling core/ synchronously on the main thread; geometry output is identical (NFR-COMPAT.1, TS-D11)
Worker imported via Vite's `new Worker(new URL(...), { type: 'module' })` pattern
userStories.notes: TECH_SPEC §7.1–7.4, TS-D9/D11. The bridge pseudocode is in TECH_SPEC §7.3 — follow it exactly. The Worker is a thin host so that the fallback (§7.4) is literally the same core/ code running synchronously; there is no separate implementation. needMesh:false requests skip the mesh build entirely — used by the no-WebGL degraded mode (PW-009) and export-only requests (PW-011). The monotonic generation counter lets stale results be discarded: if result.generation < current generation, drop it. There is exactly one geometry code path for preview and export (TS-D1, FR-VIZ.4).

userStories.title: 3D scene, fin selection & 2D inspector
userStories.description: Build the Three.js scene with orbit controls and fin selection, the WebGL degraded mode, and the 2D slat-profile inspector that renders the identical fitted path as the SVG export.
acceptanceCriteria: three/scene.ts: perspective camera, warm key + cool fill lighting (honey-oak read), OrbitControls with touch enabled, canvas resize handler; frames the default landing design on first mesh
three/fins.ts: wraps the merged BufferGeometry in one draw call; a second overlay mesh for the selected fin with highlight material
three/picking.ts: raycast merged mesh → faceIndex → binary-search finRanges → fin index (FR-VIZ.6)
Fin-index stepper in the viewport overlay (`[ 014 ▸ ] / 037`); clicking a fin in 3D updates the stepper and vice versa; selection state is shared with the 2D inspector
WebGL detection on startup: if absent, hide 3D panel and show non-blocking message; all Worker requests issued with needMesh:false; 2D inspector and export remain fully functional

Inspector2D.svelte renders the FittedPath for the selected fin from ComputeResult.paths — never recomputed separately; back edge as datum, wave front as gold stroke with gradient fill, ticks and depth callout, fin header showing fin index and x_i
userStories.notes: FR-VIZ.1/.3/.6, TECH_SPEC §8.1–8.5, TS-D5/D6, DESIGN §5.7–5.8. The 2D inspector rendering the identical FittedPath (not a recompute) is what makes V-6 structural rather than a property to police (TECH_SPEC §8.4). The auto-orbit on load shows depth and stops on first user interaction (DESIGN §6). Blueprint grid behind the canvas and warm gold-glow behind the piece (DESIGN §8) are part of this milestone. 3D material intent: --wave-mid base, low metalness, medium roughness, --wave-highlight specular on crests, --wave-shadow in troughs (DESIGN §8). Degraded mode (SRS OI-5, TECH_SPEC §8.5): keep the crosshairs/grid in the viewport region so it doesn't read as a crash.

userStories.title: Svelte UI & state
userStories.description: Wire up the full Svelte 5 component tree: the Design store with two-tier derived state, all parameter controls, readouts, validation display, and the export button.
acceptanceCriteria: state/design.svelte.ts: Design runes store; cheap derived (N, margins, full validation, exportEnabled) computed synchronously from core/ — never waiting on the Worker; expensive derived (observed depth range, total segment count) from ComputeResult
App.svelte: three-column layout — 360px control rail · 1fr viewport (min 560px) · 320px right column — plus 64px header; hairline dividers (--edge), not box borders
UnitToggle.svelte: mm | inch two-segment switch in header; toggling reformats all displayed values without altering stored mm values or causing layout shift
ParamPanel.svelte: collapsible groups (Dimensions, Wave Function, Fit Tolerance); each param as labeled row — slider + editable numeric + unit; no silent clamping (FR-IN.5)
Wave-family tabs (Diagonal · Radial · Interference) swap param region on switch; panel shows exactly the active family's params and no others (FR-IN.3)

Interference Sources editor: K∈[1,8] collapsible source rows with type-select, weight slider, family params, add/remove controls; all-weights-zero hard block flags Sources header; per-source λ≤0 flags that source's λ field
Readouts.svelte: fin count N as hero readout; spanned width, margin, stock thickness, declared depth range, actual depth used (with under-use visual), total footprint; tabular figures, live updates
ValidationList.svelte: hard-block rows (✕ + danger bg + exact SRS message + field flag) and soft-warning rows (⚠ + warn bg); 'Ready to export.' in --ok when all clear
ExportButton.svelte: disabled (no glow, not-allowed) when any hard block active; shows 'packing N slats' affordance during zip build
Landing default design rendered on first paint without user input: interference K=2, src1 diagonal θ=30° λ=300mm, src2 radial centered λ=200mm, equal weights (SRS §1.7-H)
userStories.notes: FR-IN.1–.5, FR-UI.1–.4, FR-VAL, FR-VIZ.2/.6, TECH_SPEC §5.2 (TS-D7), DESIGN §4–§5. The cheap/expensive split in the store (TS-D7) is critical: exportEnabled and all hard-block validation must update instantly without any Worker round-trip so the Export button never feels laggy. The expensive tier (observed depth range FR-IN.4, segment count FR-VAL.8) is one compute round-trip behind the slider — that is intentional and acceptable. All values stored in mm; the unit toggle only changes formatting (TS-D8). Fin selection is a single shared state driving 3D highlight, the index stepper, and the 2D inspector simultaneously (FR-VIZ.6).

userStories.title: Export pipeline
userStories.description: Build the manifest writer and zip bundler that deliver a correctly named, correctly scaled, single-download zip of per-slat SVGs + the JSON manifest.
acceptanceCriteria: export/manifest.ts: produces parawave-design.json with every parameter, chosen display unit, computed N, full wave/source config, app version, ISO export date

export/zip.ts: uses jszip to bundle all slat SVGs + manifest; filenames zero-padded to max(3, digits(N)), left→right order so lexical sort = assembly order; single .zip download triggered from ExportButton
Export issues a needMesh:false ComputeRequest (or reuses latest paths) and runs core/ at full fidelity regardless of preview throttling
No engrave layer, holes, or slots in any slat SVG (FR-EXP.5)
userStories.notes: FR-EXP.1–.9, FR-VIZ.4. FR-EXP.3: filename zero-padding uses max(3, digits(N)) — e.g. for N=37 the pad width is 3 (slat_001…slat_037); for N=1200 it is 4 (slat_0001…slat_1200). FR-EXP.7/TS-D2: the manifest's timestamp and app-version are explicitly exempt from the within-tolerance determinism guarantee. FR-EXP.8: the manifest is one-way provenance (not a load feature) — no import/restore capability is needed or wanted in v1. The export always recomputes at full fidelity (FR-VIZ.4, TS-D1) — it cannot reuse a throttled-preview result. Export must be disabled while any hard block is active (FR-UI.3, exportEnabled derived state).

userStories.title: Visual design & polish
userStories.description: Apply the full DESIGN.md visual language — CSS tokens, typography, layout density, slider styling, viewport atmosphere, motion, responsive layout, and accessibility — so the app reads as a 'Workshop Instrument', not a generic web form.
acceptanceCriteria: All CSS custom properties in :root match DESIGN §2.1 tokens; components reference tokens only, no raw hex
Fraunces used for wordmark and section headers only; IBM Plex Mono used for all controls, labels, readouts, and values; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums on all numeric outputs
Three-column layout: 360px rail, 1fr viewport, 320px right column, 64px header, 8px base grid, hairline (--edge) dividers
Sliders: 2px track, --gold fill to thumb, diamond/square thumb with --gold-glow on hover/focus, --danger track on invalid state; keyboard-operable (arrows, Home/End)
3D viewport: corner crosshairs in --cool, blueprint grid (--grid minor / --grid-strong major), warm --gold-glow radial behind the canvas, film-grain overlay at --grain-opacity
Page-load reveal animation: header → rail stagger → crosshairs → piece fade-up; gentle auto-orbit stops on first interaction; @media (prefers-reduced-motion) disables animations

Responsive breakpoints: full three-column ≥1200px; narrow columns 820–1199px; tabbed instrument panel 600–819px (Controls / Inspector / Readouts); non-broken fallback <600px; 44px touch targets on tablet
All text/control pairs pass WCAG AA: --ink-dim on --panel; gold-on-charcoal large text; state conveyed by icon + text + color (never color alone)
Every control has a visible --type-label and an accessible name; aria-live on readouts and validation; logical tab order; 2px --gold-bright focus-visible ring on every interactive element
userStories.notes: DESIGN §1–§10, NFR-A11Y.1/.2. Anti-slop clause (DESIGN §1.3, non-negotiable): no Inter/Roboto/Arial/system-UI fonts; no purple gradients or blue-on-white SaaS palettes; no light/white theme; no pill buttons with drop shadows; no emoji as iconography. The palette is dominant charcoal + sharp gold accent. Open issues to resolve during this milestone: DI-1 (final hex after WCAG AA audit), DI-2 (Fraunces opsz for warmth without decoration), DI-3 (grain overlay render cost — drop to static tiled asset if it affects framerate). The 3D material (PW-009) is revisited here to confirm it reads as honey-oak against the warm background. Reduced-motion: @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) must disable the load stagger, auto-orbit, and validation flash; state changes become instant. Functionality must be identical with or without motion.

userStories.title: Tests & verification
userStories.description: Write the full Vitest test suite covering all SRS §9 verification items (V-1…V-6) and run the manual Carbide Create import checklist.
acceptanceCriteria: Property test: f ∈ [−1, 1] for diagonal, radial, and interference with random weights (FR-WAVE contract)
Property test: p ≤ D, f=−1 ⇒ p=pMin, f=+1 ⇒ p=D for random Design inputs (FR-GEO.3)
Property test: front-edge max deviation ≤ fitTolerance via dense resampling for each wave family (V-4, NFR-ACCURACY.1)
Property test: each slat path is closed; back/top/bottom edges are line segments; front edge consists of cubic Béziers (FR-EXP.2)
Unit test: mm→inch→mm round-trip returns the original value with no drift (V-2, FR-IN.2)
Unit test: re-fitting identical parameters produces paths that agree within fitTolerance on the same engine — byte-identical (V-3 per TS-D2)
Golden tests: fixed reference designs snapshot-compared numerically within tolerance across all three wave families
Unit test: exported filenames sort lexically to left→right assembly order; zero-pad width is max(3, digits(N)) (FR-EXP.3)
Table-driven test: each FR-VAL.1–.11 condition produces the correct tier (hard/soft), exact SRS message, and correct exportEnabled value (V-5)
Unit test: 2D inspector path data and exported SVG path data for the same fin are geometrically equivalent (V-6, FR-VIZ.3)
Component test: family-aware panel shows exactly the active family's params; switching families swaps params cleanly (FR-IN.3)
Component test: Export button disabled when any hard block active, enabled otherwise (FR-UI.3)

MANUAL V-1 — Carbide Create import: export a known interference design; import each slat SVG into Carbide Create; confirm correct physical size (H × depth), upright orientation, single clean closed vector, no repair needed
MANUAL smoke test: full happy path (PRD §11) — land → set units → adjust dimensions → Interference wave → orbit 3D → inspect fin 2D → Export → open zip → verify filenames, manifest, SVG count
MANUAL: soft performance warning appears and export still works at N > 400 fins (FR-VAL.6)
MANUAL: WebGL-absent degraded mode — 3D panel shows message; 2D inspector and export still function (TECH_SPEC §8.5)
userStories.notes: TECH_SPEC §12, SRS §9. All automated tests run headless in CI via Vitest — the pure core/ makes this possible without a browser or GPU. Numerical comparisons use within-tolerance checks (not byte-diff) per TS-D2. Open issues that must be resolved before this milestone can pass: OI-2 (confirm 0.05mm default / 0.001mm floor against Shapeoko/Nomad precision via V-1); OI-3 (confirm K=8 cap reproduces wave.jpg look); OI-6 (tune FIN_WARN=400 and SEGMENT_WARN≈50000 from profiling); OI-new SEED_PER_WAVELENGTH and MAX_DEPTH validated via the front-edge deviation property test. V-1 (Carbide Create import) is the critical manual gate — it validates the entire SVG export chain (FR-EXP.1/.2/.6, §1.7-A/B) and cannot be automated.
